daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Indonesian parliament reaffirmed that the Hajj and Umrah Law does not criminalize independent umrah pilgrims, addressing concerns over recent legislative changes. President Prabowo issued a presidential decree establishing seven new district prosecutor's offices, expanding prosecutorial capacity nationwide. The president also instructed that Danantara be involved in every decision of the Financial System Stability Committee (KSSK), strengthening the state holding company's role in financial policymaking.

  • PSI announced that Kaesang Pangarep will contest Central Java electoral district V as a DPR candidate, with the party citing his upbringing in Solo as the rationale for the choice and expressing ambitions to make Central Java a PSI stronghold.
  • The KPK detained East Java DPRD member Moch Mahrus as a suspect in a grant fund case, after he allegedly gave Rp 1.5 billion and 1 kg of gold to a DPR member to secure community group grant funds.
  • A DPR member from the PAN faction, A Bakri, passed away, the legislature confirmed.
  • Coordinating Minister Zulkifli Hasan announced that the Rp 1.8 trillion budget for "kipas angin" (fan) allocations to village cooperatives will be audited by the Supreme Audit Agency (BPK).
  • A DPR member requested the government prepare risk mitigation measures regarding social assistance distribution through village cooperatives.
  • PDI-P chairwoman Megawati Soekarnoputri met with Cambodia's deputy prime minister and explained the history and application of Pancasila ideology.
  • A NasDem legislator rejected a new portal for monitoring the Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) program, citing specific concerns about the system.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The DPR called for a special task force to secure the release of four Indonesian citizens held hostage by Somali pirates. Indonesia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported that no Indonesian nationals were reported injured following a 7.1 magnitude earthquake in Kumamoto, Japan, and the Indonesian embassy urged citizens to follow local authorities' instructions.

  • Indonesia and China agreed to discuss housing technology cooperation, expanding bilateral ties in the construction sector.
  • Following a meeting with Coordinating Minister Airlangga Hartarto, China expressed confidence that Indonesia will protect Chinese companies operating in the country.
  • A Chinese military attaché stated that Indonesia-China defence cooperation is growing stronger, highlighting military-to-military ties.
  • Japan granted zero-percent tariffs to Indonesian processed tuna exports, boosting trade relations.
  • Indonesia and Australia partnered on modern irrigation projects in Kalimantan, strengthening development cooperation.

Other

President Prabowo convened a meeting to prepare for El Niño and forest fire risks, ordering regional governments to strengthen disaster mitigation as BMKG confirmed that Indonesia has entered strong El Niño conditions. The meteorology agency plans to fill reservoirs and conduct weather modification to address potential drought. Energy Minister Bahlil assured that subsidized fuel and LPG prices would not increase, confirming also that Indonesia is importing Russian oil to strengthen energy security.

  • The Cooperatives Ministry announced that village cooperative managers' salaries will be funded from the state budget (APBN) for two years.
  • Indonesia aims to pass a new Cooperatives Law this year, updating the regulatory framework for the sector.
  • The Ministry of Manpower confirmed the government will address planned layoffs at garment companies in Central Java.
  • The Health Ministry issued regulations limiting intern doctors' working hours to a maximum of 40 hours per week.
  • Bareskrim exposed distribution methods for "gas whip pink" narcotics via WhatsApp, including "buy 5 get 1 free" promotions.
